info.name: Girder REST API (Emory Digital Slide Archive) annotation resource API
resource
Delete a set of items, folders, or other resources.

params.name: resources
params.description: A JSON-encoded set of resources to delete. Each type is a list of ids.  For example: {"item": [(item id 1), (item id2)], "folder": [(folder id 1)]}.

params.name: progress
params.description: Whether to record progress on this task.

items.docs: Delete a set of items, folders, or other resources.

info.name: Copy a set of items and folders.

params.name: resources
params.description: A JSON-encoded set of resources to copy. Each type is a list of ids.  Only folders and items may be specified.  For example: {"item": [(item id 1), (item id2)], "folder": [(folder id 1)]}.

params.name: parentType
params.description: Parent type for the new parent of these resources.

params.name: parentId
params.description: Parent ID for the new parent of these resources.

params.name: progress
params.description: Whether to record progress on this task.

params.name: copyAnnotations
params.description: Copy annotations when copying resources (default true)

items.docs: Copy a set of items and folders.

info.name: Download a set of items, folders, collections, and users as a zip archive.

params.name: resources
params.description: A JSON-encoded set of resources to download. Each type is a list of ids. For example: {"item": [(item id 1), (item id 2)], "folder": [(folder id 1)]}.

params.name: includeMetadata
params.description: Include any metadata in JSON files in the archive.

items.docs: This route is also exposed via the POST method because the request parameters can be quite long, and encoding them in the URL (as is standard when using the GET method) can cause the URL to become too long, which causes errors.

info.name: Look up a resource in the data hierarchy by path.

params.name: path
params.description: The path of the resource.  The path must be an absolute Unix path starting with either "/user/[user name]", for a user's resources or "/collection/[collection name]", for resources under a collection.

items.docs: Look up a resource in the data hierarchy by path.

info.name: Set metadata on multiple resources at once.

params.name: resources
params.description: A JSON-encoded set of resources to modify.  Each type is a list of ids. For example: {"item": [(item id 1), (item id 2)], "folder": [(folder id 1)]}.

params.name: allowNull
params.description: Whether "null" is allowed as a metadata value.

items.docs: Set metadata on multiple resources at once.

params.name: parentType
params.description: Parent type for the new parent of these resources.

params.description: Parent ID for the new parent of these resources.

params.description: Whether to record progress on this task.

info.name: Redirect to a model endpoint based on a resource path

params.name: path
params.description: The path of the resource.  The path must be an absolute Unix path starting with either "/user/[user name]", for a user's resources or "/collection/[collection name]", for resources under a collection.

items.docs: This is significantly less efficient that using /(model)/(id)/..., as the route must validated and tested to that the longest sensible path is used.

info.name: Search for resources in the system.

params.name: q
params.description: The search query.

params.name: mode
params.description: The search mode. Can always use either a text search or a prefix-based search.

params.name: types
params.description: A JSON list of resource types to search for, e.g. ["user", "folder", "item"].

params.name: level
params.description: Minimum required access level.

params.name: limit
params.description: Result set size limit.

params.name: offset
params.description: Offset into result set.
